 COLUMBIA, S.C. (WACH) - With the November 3 election just two days away, we're looking at the choices facing South Carolina voter and the women helping shape those choices.
 Former state senator Katrina Shealy spent 12 years representing Lexington County as a Republican and became nationally known as one of South Carolina's bipartisan *sister senators* who broke party lines by challenging abortion restrictions in the state.
 In the wake of that, Shealy and other female GOP lawmakers who challenged the party, lost their re-election bids, but she hasn't stepped away from politics.
 Now she's crossing party lines with several endorsements and continuing to speak out on issues affecting South Carolina, including affordability, good governance, and women, children and family issues.
 Shealy is endorsing Democrat for governor Jermaine Johnson, as well as Democrat Vincent Coe in the state treasurer's race against incumber Republican, Curtis Loftis.
